matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) to ensure the resulting symbols are valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, verify you are not rotating it to a different orientation.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick and placing it as a vertical stick, which creates an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, ensure you will only relocate a single stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and not placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After deciding a stick move, check each character for validity.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a corrected equation, verify the numeric equality.
matchstick.example: Accepting an equation that looks plausible but does not satisfy the numeric equality, such as XVI = XIX - III.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain both diagonals, otherwise the character becomes invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a diagonal stick from an X or V, ensure you either keep both diagonals or replace the missing one within the same move.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid character.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of your response, before submitting.
matchstick.example: Providing the answer without the required final line or with extra spaces.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change can be achieved by moving exactly one stick, preserving orientation and not altering any other sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you think you have a solution, double‑check that only one stick was moved.
matchstick.example: Changing multiple sticks or rotating a stick, resulting in more than one stick moved.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (a single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave an empty placeholder.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from an I.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from I and leaving a blank space.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick to or from an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from a + sign and not adding it elsewhere, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator transformation patterns
matchstick.principle: When the equation contains both = and - (or a +), consider moving a horizontal stick from = to - (or vice versa) to swap them, or moving the vertical stick from + to create an I, turning + into - and adding a numeral. These specific operator transformations often resolve the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the arithmetic is close but off by a small amount and the puzzle includes =, - or +, try swapping operators or converting + to - while creating an I.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from = to - but leaving = as a single horizontal line (invalid) – the correct move swaps = and - so both remain valid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks only the visual validity of characters and forgets to ensure the numeric equality holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a corrected equation, convert both sides to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the equation content and neglects the required final line format.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with the exact line 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' using uppercase letters and collapsing whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When you take a stick from a character, immediately decide where to place it to form another valid character or operator.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral without ensuring the remaining parts still form a valid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick from a numeral, check that the numeral can remain valid or that the stick will be added back within the same move.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks without checking Roman numeral syntax rules, leading to numerals that violate standard conventions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that each numeral follows Roman numeral rules (no more than three consecutive I's, correct subtractive notation, proper ordering).
